still: Brandon sits on the third step of a narrow shared stairwell in a rented house, elbows on his knees, head bowed to the phone in his hands, its pale light the only warm thing on his face. A bare bulb on the landing above throws a hard cone of yellow light, and the walls are scuffed magnolia with a row of mismatched coat hooks and a stack of unopened post on the bottom stair. The picture is taken from a lens fixed high in the corner of the ceiling above the landing, looking down and across the stairs, a washed-out, compressed, slightly grainy video frame with muted colour and soft shadows, as if on cheap night-mode sensor footage. Brandon is small in the frame, seen from above. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon sits hunched on the stair with the phone held close, then pushes both palms on his knees and stands up in one decisive motion, his brow set, jaw tight, eyes fixed on the front door below. Later he settles his weight onto his front foot and glances once towards the door with his eyelids narrowed. The bare bulb on the landing flickers faintly. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: a bulb buzzing, a trainer squeaking on a stair tread, the creak of the banister, a distant television through a wall. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A wide-angle view from a doorbell mounted beside a front door, looking out at the doorway of a terraced house: the door stands open onto a dim hallway with a bicycle leaning against a radiator. Jenny stands in the doorway on the left of the frame with her arms folded and her brows pulled together, her mouth flat, eyes fixed on Brandon. Brandon stands on the right of the frame on the doorstep, his shoulders open, brows slightly raised, already half turning his body away towards the street. The lens bulges slightly at the edges, daylight from the street is blown out to white behind the doorframe, and the colour is flat and compressed with fine video noise. A chipped boot scraper and a wilted plant in a margarine tub sit by the step. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Jenny keeps her arms folded in the doorway on the left while Brandon, on the right, finishes turning his shoulders to the street and takes one step away. Later Jenny shifts her weight onto her other foot and her eyes follow him. The wilted plant sways slightly in a light breeze. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: a car passing on the road, shoes on a stone step, wind against the doorbell microphone, a bicycle bell ticking as the door shifts. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: The same wide-angle doorbell view, a little later: Jenny has stepped out over the threshold onto the stone doorstep on the left of the frame, a thick stack of folded leaflets in one hand, her head tilted back and her eyes narrowed as she sizes Brandon up. Brandon is on the right of the frame, his body turning back towards her, brows lifted, mouth a little open. The lens bulges at its edges, the sky behind them is a flat bleached white, the colours are washed out and compressed, and the hallway behind Jenny is a murky dark. A pair of wet wellies stands against the wall by the door. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Jenny holds the leaflets out a few inches towards Brandon with her chin lifted, and Brandon completes his turn and faces her with his eyebrows high. Later she lowers the leaflets and her eyes flick over his shoulder at the street. The wet wellies drip slowly onto the step. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: paper rustling, shoes shuffling on the stone, a dog barking down the road, the hum of a distant van. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A draughty village community hall seen from a lens fixed high in a corner near the ceiling, looking down the length of the room. Stackable plastic chairs are piled in leaning towers against the wall, a trestle table holds a plate of plain biscuits and a catering urn, and six or seven campaigners in anoraks sit around a cluster of tables, one older woman with a ring binder, one man with his finger raised mid-argument. Brandon crosses the foreground carrying four chairs stacked against his chest, his face bright with delight, his eyebrows high and his mouth wide in a grin. The light is flat fluorescent tube light with a green cast, the colour washed out and compressed, and the floor is scuffed pale wood. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. The campaigners gesture and talk over each other at the tables while Brandon walks steadily from the right of the frame to the left carrying the stack of chairs, grinning. Later he stops, shifts the stack on his chest and looks round for where to put it, his eyes wide. One fluorescent tube flickers overhead. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: the scrape of plastic chair legs on wood, a tea urn ticking as it heats, overlapping muffled voices, a tube light buzzing. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A cheap pub on a weekday evening, seen from a lens mounted high above the bar and looking down across the room at a small corner table. Brandon sits on the left of the frame, leaning slightly forward with one finger resting beside his ear, his brows drawn together in concentration and his eyes on Jenny. Jenny sits on the right of the frame, talking with her hands open, her brows raised and her mouth mid-word. Two glasses of lager and a second round of drinks stand on the sticky table between them, with a bag of crisps ripped open flat. A fruit machine glows in the background. The light is dim orange pub lamplight, the picture is washed-out, grainy and compressed, and the bar top foreground is out of focus. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Jenny talks and gestures with her open hands while Brandon listens, his finger at his ear and his eyes fixed on her face, then nods slowly. Later Jenny picks up her drink, leans back in her chair and stays where she is, settling in. The fruit machine pulses with coloured light in the background. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: the thrum of a pub room, glasses clinking, the fruit machine jingling, a chair leg scraping on a sticky floor. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A community hall packed with about forty people on folding chairs, seen from a lens fixed high at the back corner of the room, looking down towards a small raised platform. Brandon stands at the front on the right of the frame with one hand held out, his chin up, his eyebrows lifted and his mouth open mid-sentence, speaking with total ease. Every head in the room is turned towards him, a sea of backs of heads, woolly hats and thinning crowns, a woman near the front leaning in with her elbow on her knee. A tea urn and a trestle table sit unattended at the side, and the strip lighting is flat and slightly green. The colour is washed out and compressed with fine video noise. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon speaks to the room with an open hand moving in a slow arc while the audience stays turned to him, and a few heads nod. Later a ripple of movement passes through the seated crowd as people lean forward and the woman near the front sits back and folds her arms, smiling. One fluorescent tube flickers over the back rows. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: a hall full of people shifting on folding chairs, a cough, the hum of a tube light, a tea urn ticking. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A cramped attic bedroom at night, seen from a lens fixed high in the corner where the sloped ceiling meets the wall, looking down at a single bed under the eaves. Brandon sits on the edge of the bed typing on his phone with both thumbs, his whole face lifted in a broad open smile, his cheeks high and his eyes bright, lit from below by the pale glow of the phone. A rail of crumpled clothes, a stack of takeaway boxes and a small skylight with a black sky behind it fill the room. The only light is the phone and a faint orange glow from a streetlamp through the skylight, the picture is grainy night-mode footage with lifted blacks and washed-out colour. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon types quickly with both thumbs, grinning at the phone, then draws a breath and lets out a small silent laugh with his shoulders shaking. Later he lowers the phone slowly to his knee and looks up at the skylight, still smiling, his eyelids soft. The streetlamp light through the skylight flickers faintly as something passes in front of it. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: thumbs tapping glass, a mattress spring creaking, a distant car on wet road, a pipe ticking in the roof. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A large bland open-plan office at night seen from a lens fixed in the ceiling directly above a row of grey desks. One woman in a cardigan, invented and ordinary, sits alone at a desk in the middle of the frame, seen from behind and above, her hand on a computer mouse and her head bent towards a monitor whose face is turned away from the camera, showing only a pale smear of light on her glasses and the desk. The rest of the room is dark apart from the green glow of a vending machine and a strip of corridor light. Grey carpet tiles, a swivel chair with a torn arm and a half-dead plant in the foreground. The colour is washed out and compressed, grainy, like a lifted dark video frame. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. The woman clicks and drags the mouse slowly down the screen, then stops, her head tilted, and holds still over one line. Later she leans back in the swivel chair and rubs the back of her neck with one hand. The vending machine light hums and pulses faintly in the dark corner. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: a mouse click, a chair creaking, the low hum of air conditioning, a vending machine compressor humming. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: The cramped attic bedroom at night, seen from a lens fixed high in the corner under the sloped ceiling, looking down at the bed. Brandon lies asleep on his back with the duvet pulled to his chest and a small contented smile on his mouth, his brows relaxed and his eyelids closed. On the cluttered bedside table a phone lies charging on a tangle of cable with one small white light glowing on its edge, beside a mug with a tea ring and a torn packet of biscuits. The room is nearly black apart from a faint orange wash of streetlight from the skylight, the picture is grainy night-mode footage, washed out and compressed. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon breathes slowly in his sleep, his chest rising and falling under the duvet, the smile held on his mouth. Later he turns his head a few degrees on the pillow and his brow twitches once before settling. The small light on the charging phone pulses slowly. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: slow breathing, the rustle of a duvet, a pipe ticking in the roof, a faint car passing outside. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: Giles on a video call, framed from a laptop webcam at the height of his chest, tilted slightly up, sitting at a kitchen table with a plastic bowl of salad in front of him and a fork in his hand. He looks down at the bowl rather than at the lens, his eyelids half lowered, his mouth working, his brows flat with boredom. Behind him a bookcase crowded with unmatched paperbacks and a box file fills the wall, and a window to one side is blown out to a white rectangle that bleaches the edge of the picture. The image is soft, low-resolution and compressed with blocky colour smearing, the colour washed out and slightly green. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Giles spears a forkful of salad, lifts it to his mouth and chews while his lips move in a drone of speech, his eyes still on the bowl. Later he pushes a leaf round the bowl with the fork and flicks his eyes up at the lens for a half second before dropping them again. The white window behind him brightens slightly as a cloud shifts. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: a fork scraping a plastic bowl, chewing, a fridge humming, a faint laptop fan whirr. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A corner table in an ordinary English pub in the afternoon, completely empty of people, seen from a lens fixed high above the bar and looking down at an angle across the room. A half-drunk pint of bitter stands on a round table with a beer mat folded under one edge, a padded stool pushed in on each side and a patch of daylight from a leaded window lying across the carpet. Brass horse-shoes on a rail, a threadbare red carpet and a dim wall lamp that is switched off. The colour is washed out and compressed, the daylight window slightly blown out, the picture grainy and soft at the edges. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Dust drifts through the shaft of daylight over the empty table while the pint sits perfectly still. Later a shadow of someone passing the window slides across the carpet and away. A slow bead of condensation runs down the pint glass. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: a quiet room tone, a clock ticking, a distant glass clinking behind the bar, a dishwasher humming. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A close high-angle view of a desk in a dim office, taken from a lens fixed in the ceiling directly above, the room lit only by the pale glow of a monitor whose face is turned slightly away from the camera, so the screen shows only a soft blur of light. In the blur a small pale rectangle, no bigger than a stamp, hints at a passport-style face photo, too small and soft to make out. The desk holds a cold mug, a wired keyboard with worn keys and a lanyard coiled beside it. Nothing legible anywhere. The picture is grainy and washed out, the corners vignetted dark and the colour compressed. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. The pale glow of the screen pulses slightly as the image on it refreshes, throwing a faint shifting light across the keyboard and the desk. Later a hand enters from the bottom edge of the frame, rests briefly on the mouse and leaves again. A thin curl of steam rises from the mug. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: a computer fan whirring, a mouse click, the hum of an air conditioner, a keyboard ticking once. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A meeting room table seen from a lens fixed high in the corner of the ceiling, looking down across the room. On the long table stands a large architectural model of an enormous windowless slab of a data centre, flat grey and the size of a coffee table, built on the edge of a little model English town with tiny terraced houses, a church spire and a roundabout. Blue plastic pipes snake from the slab across the green baize landscape towards a model reservoir. Around the table are empty swivel chairs and a flipchart with its pages left blank. The light is flat office strip light, the colour is washed out and compressed, and the picture is grainy with a slight fish-eye curve at the corners. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. A beam of weak afternoon sun creeps slowly across the model town from the left, lighting the tiny houses one row at a time. Later the fluorescent light overhead dips and recovers, and the blue pipes catch a brief highlight. A blind slat in the window ticks softly against the frame. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Audio: air conditioning hum, a blind slat tapping, a fluorescent tube buzzing, a distant phone ringing in another room. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.
